findings.problem: "Holy One" in the quote from the Psalms (Acts 13:35, “You will not let Your Holy One see decay.”) has no definition. It is a title, and a reader who doesn't know who it means can't follow how Paul uses the Psalm to point to Jesus.

rule.text: If not knowing the word would make it harder to understand what is being said, define it.

findings.problem: "fulfilled" (on stop 2 cards 9 and 15) has no definition. Both sentences depend on it: the rulers "fulfilled the words of the prophets" (Acts 13:27), and God "has fulfilled" His promise by raising Jesus (Acts 13:32-33). In this sense the word means made a prophecy or promise come true, which a younger reader may not know.

rule.text: If not knowing the word would make it harder to understand what is being said, define it.

findings.problem: "testifies" (God "testifies about him", Acts 13:22) has no definition. The sentence is about God speaking publicly in favor of David, and that is unclear without the word.

rule.text: If not knowing the word would make it harder to understand what is being said, define it.

findings.problem: Proper names are not treated the same way. "Canaan" and "Pilate" get pop-ups, but other places and people on the cards get none: Paphos, Perga, Pamphylia and Pisidian Antioch (1.1, 1.3), Iconium (3.17 answer), Samuel, Kish, Benjamin and Jesse (2.3-2.6), Galilee (2.14 answer) and Barnabas (3.1). The docs don't say whether proper names count as hard words.
findings.question: Should place names and people's names get definition pop-ups? If so, which ones: all of them, or only the ones a reader needs to follow the story?
